misconceptions.description: Justifying an AI tool by its efficiency while skipping the learning purpose it is supposed to serve
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts a tool because it is fast or consistent without stating what learning goal it advances
misconceptions.feedback: State the learning purpose first. Efficiency is only defensible once the tool clearly serves a specific learning goal.

misconceptions.description: Reaching a decision using only one lens (only equity, or only privacy) instead of integrating the module's tools
misconceptions.trigger: learner's capstone map applies one check and ignores stakeholders, consent, or the negotiated decision
misconceptions.feedback: Integrate the lenses. A capstone decision should run the stakeholder, privacy and consent, and negotiated-decision checks together.

misconceptions.description: Presenting a final decision with no record of an alternative that was considered and rejected for a reason
misconceptions.trigger: learner states a conclusion but never shows what they ruled out
misconceptions.feedback: Record at least one rejected option and why. A defensible judgment shows the alternative it turned down.
